plausibility.summary: Secondary pentaradial symmetry from a bilateral ancestor is a well-trodden evolutionary path on Earth; a decentralized nerve ring with no true head fits intertidal reef and tide-pool habitats (F13, F21) where threats and food arrive from all bearings. Slightly higher gravity (F2) does not block this in water or when the disc is supported on rock; it mainly punishes fast terrestrial sprinting, which matches a sluggish radial crawler. Island radiation from marine founders (F27) can produce a recognisably echinoderm-like lineage without copying Spore. Highly speculative only if the same biochemistry (F24) must share recent ancestry with land quadrupeds—that is a game graft rule, not a natural-history requirement.
fixes: Secondary pentaradial symmetry from a bilateral ancestor is a well-trodden evolutionary path on Earth; a decentralized nerve ring with no true head fits intertidal reef and tide-pool habitats (F13, F21) where threats and food arrive from all bearings. Slightly higher gravity (F2) does not block this in water or when the disc is supported on rock; it mainly punishes fast terrestrial sprinting, which matches a sluggish radial crawler. Island radiation from marine founders (F27) can produce a recognisably echinoderm-like lineage without copying Spore. Highly speculative only if the same biochemistry (F24) must share recent ancestry with land quadrupeds—that is a game graft rule, not a natural-history requirement.

relations.note: (council kind 'Predator-Prey') Brújula sacrifices arms to distract Garfio; Garfio's strong bite often severs limbs, but the crawler's radial arms make it harder to swallow whole.
(council kind 'Commensal') Follows Rondo herds to scavenged carcasses; Rondo ignores the low-value radial crawler as it cleans hide-bound tissue.
(council kind 'Habitat') Nests in the Coloso's massive scale pools; benefits from the giant's tidal shadow and the shelter of the islet's dyke.

body_plan.origin: secondary radialisation from a crawling bilateral ancestor

temperament: Patient, territorial over prime pools, highly resilient to physical trauma
secrets: Regenerated arm tips store trace minerals; harvesting yields bone shards and salt crystals.
The central nerve ring can be stunned by rapid temperature drops, revealing a dormant egg-nest in the pool below.
moments: On spring low tide, a colony seals into the rock crevice. Their arms retract inward, the tube feet lock, and the disc hardens like polished stone. The tide recedes, leaving a ring of silent, waiting statues until the next swell returns.

journal.en: No face. No back. Just five equal claims on the world.
They cut themselves loose. The sea gives it back, slow but sure.
